Subject: Encryption key custody & subprocessor handling — DPA redline question

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for walking through the DPA last week. We’re reviewing the subprocessor and key-custody sections and have two narrow asks before we send back a marked-up DPA: 

1) Escrow / recovery: you reference a vendor-managed key-escrow option in the annex (pg. 7). Can you confirm whether Medicor intends to require us to use a Medicor-designated escrow provider, or whether Redwood can propose an escrow arrangement (we have an audited partner we prefer)? If Medicor requires a specific vendor, please share the attestation / SOC-like evidence you have so we can scope the integration.

2) Key split & HSM requirement: The current draft says keys must be stored in a KEK-protected HSM for certain data classes. We need to confirm which PII categories trigger the HSM mandate (e.g., PHI vs. pseudonymous identifiers). For lower-sensitivity PII we can offer envelope encryption with key-splitting and multi-party control instead of full HSM.

Attached is a short proposal describing two implementation options (vendor escrow vs. Redwood-managed escrow with split custody). Could you have security@medicorhealth.com take a quick look and tell us whether one of these meets your procurement/compliance constraints?

If helpful we can book a 30-min call today to align on phrasing so the redline reflects the right operational constraints.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Mina — thanks for the clear notes and the proposal. Forwarding to our security ops team (cc’d) for the technical attestation. Quick answers while they review: 

• Medicor does not require a single designated escrow vendor by policy; we do require the escrow provider to have at least SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 evidence and to support split-key recovery where recovery keys require multi-person authorization.
• HSM requirement: currently the DPA language is intended to apply to PHI and any PII that is uniquely identifiable and used for clinical decisioning. For analytics-only pseudonymous identifiers we can accept envelope encryption with split custody and audited key handling controls.

I attached a vendor attestation we received earlier this year from a certified escrow partner that aligns with our baseline (vendor-attestation-2026-09-24.pdf). Once security confirms the specifics we can align on redline text.

Olivia
Director, InfoSec — Medicor Health

Olivia / Mina — looping in legal counsel. Thanks for the quick answer, Olivia. 

From a contract standpoint, we propose the following narrow redline snippet for the key custody paragraph to capture both HSM and split-custody options: 

"Where data is classified as PHI or is used for clinical decisioning, Supplier shall store encryption keys in an HSM that meets FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or equivalent and shall provide Medicor with attestations of HSM administration practices. For non-decisioning, pseudonymized PII, Supplier may instead use envelope encryption with a split-key escrow arrangement, where no single party has unilateral access to plaintext and where escrow providers maintain SOC 2 Type II certification. Supplier shall document key-splitting, recovery, and access approval workflows and provide Medicor with reasonable evidence upon request."

A couple of follow-ups we need to confirm with your security team before we send a marked redline back: 
1) Is Medicor comfortable accepting Redwood’s preferred escrow partner if we furnish the SOC2 / ISO evidence (Oliviasaid likely yes, but we need confirmation from security).
2) Do you need DocuSign-level signature on an escrow SLA (we can provide a standard DocuSign agreement) or will a PO + signed DPA suffice?

I attached a redline with the proposed language for your review (redline_DPA_sections.docx). If your security team provides a short bullet list of mandatory attestations (e.g., annual penetration test, key rotation cadence), we will incorporate that into the annex.
